sect2.title: Introduction to D-Bus
sect2.para: Even though D-Bus was built in LFS, there are some features provided by the package that other GLFS packages need, but their dependencies didn't fit into LFS.
D-Bus was already compiled before, but not a useful program, dbus-launch. This pass will cover it, and some setup required.

sect3.title: Configuration Information
sect3.para: The configuration files listed above should probably not be modified. If changes are required, you should create /etc/dbus-1/session-local.conf and/or /etc/dbus-1/system-local.conf and make any desired changes to these files.

If any packages install a D-Bus .service file outside of the standard /usr/share/dbus-1/services directory, that directory should be added to the local session configuration. For instance, /usr/local/share/dbus-1/services can be added by performing the following commands as the root user:

screen.userinput:
cat > /etc/dbus-1/session-local.conf << "EOF" <!DOCTYPE busconfig PUBLIC "-//freedesktop//DTD D-BUS Bus Configuration 1.0//EN" "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/dbus/1.0/busconfig.dtd"> <busconfig>
<!-- Search for .service files in /usr/local --> <servicedir>/usr/local/share/dbus-1/services</servicedir>
</busconfig> EOF

sect3.title: D-Bus Session Daemon
sect3.para:
To automatically start dbus-daemon when the system is rebooted, install the /etc/rc.d/init.d/dbus bootscript from the
blfs-bootscripts package.
To automatically start dbus-daemon when the system is rebooted, create and enable the OpenRC service:
Note that this serviceboot script only starts the system-wide D-Bus daemon. Each user requiring access to D-Bus services will also need to run a session daemon as well.
You can install a user service for D-Bus as the &root; user:

screen.userinput:
&install-exec; /dev/stdin /etc/user/init.d/dbus << "EOF" #!/sbin/openrc-run # Starts a D-Bus user session # Authors: Zeckma - zeckma@linuxfromscratch.com # Version: LFS &version;
description="starts a dbus user session"
supervisor=supervise-daemon dbus_socket="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/bus" export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=$dbus_socket" command="/usr/bin/dbus-daemon" command_args="--session --syslog --nofork --address ${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS}"
start_post() { echo "export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS}" > ~/.config/rc/env/dbus.env } EOF

sect3.para: As a regular user, enable the service:

There are many methods you can use to start a session daemon using the dbus-launch command. Review the dbus-launch man page for details about the available parameters and options. Here are some suggestions and examples:

There are many methods you can use to start a session daemon using the dbus-launch command. Review the dbus-launch man page for details about the available parameters and options. Here are some suggestions and examples:

listitem.para: Add dbus-launch to the line in the ~/.xinitrc file that starts your graphical desktop environment.

If you use gdm or some other display manager that calls the ~/.xsession file, you can add dbus-launch to the line in your ~/.xsession file that starts your graphical desktop environment. The syntax would be similar to the example in the ~/.xinitrc file.

The examples shown previously use dbus-launch to specify a program to be run. This has the benefit (when also using the --exit-with-x11 parameter) of stopping the session daemon when the specified program is stopped. You can also start the session daemon in your system or personal startup scripts by adding the following lines:

userinput.literal: # Start the D-Bus session daemon eval `dbus-launch` export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS

listitem.para: This method will not stop the session daemon when you exit your shell, therefore you should add the following line to your ~/.bash_logout file:

userinput.literal: # Kill the D-Bus session daemon kill $DBUS_SESSION_BUS_PID

sect3.para: Now would be a good idea to reboot and test to see if D-Bus, elogind, etc. works, and you can login. Run the command loginctl after ensuring D-Bus is running. The result should indicate that a SESSION and a SEAT have been created.
